facts.statement: The genus Barbosania was named and described by Ross A. Elgin and Eberhard Frey in 2011.
facts.quote: Barbosania was named and described by Ross A. Elgin and Eberhard Frey in 2011

facts.statement: The generic name Barbosania honors Professor Miguel Barbosa of the Museu de História Natural de Sintra, whose collection holds the type specimen.
facts.quote: The generic name honours Professor Miguel Barbosa of the Portuguese Museu de História Natural de Sintra in whose collection the type specimen is present

facts.statement: The holotype consists of an almost complete, partially articulated, and uncompressed skeleton including the skull.
facts.quote: It consists of an almost complete skeleton including the skull, that is partially articulated and uncompressed

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was prepared at the Staatliches Museum für Naturkunde Karlsruhe in Germany.
facts.quote: The specimen was prepared in the German Staatliches Museum für Naturkunde Karlsruhe

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that several specimens previously assigned to Brasileodactylus might actually belong to Barbosania.
facts.quote: Several specimens previously referred to Brasileodactylus may instead be individuals of Barbosania

facts.statement: Barbosania is an extinct pterosaur from the Aptian to Albian stages of the Romualdo Formation in northeastern Brazil.
facts.quote: Barbosania is an extinct genus of crestless targaryendraconian pterosaur from the Cretaceous Romualdo Formation of the Santana Group of northeastern Brazil, dating to the Aptian to Albian

facts.statement: Barbosania was a medium-sized pterodactyloid with a skull measuring 392 millimeters (15.4 inches) in length.
facts.quote: Barbosania was a medium-sized pterodactyloid with a skull length of 392 millimetres, or 15.4 inches

facts.statement: The body length of Barbosania was 209.5 millimeters (8.2 inches).
facts.quote: Its body was 209.5 millimetres, or 8.2 inches long

facts.statement: The skull of Barbosania is elongated with a slight upward curve in the snout.
facts.quote: The skull is elongated with a slight upwards bend in the snout

facts.statement: Barbosania lacks a rostral and dentary median sagittal crest, distinguishing it from related pterosaurs.
facts.quote: Its lack of a rostral and dentary median sagittal crest allows a distinction from other related pterosaurs

facts.statement: Barbosania possesses thirteen dorsal vertebrae, a unique trait distinguishing it from the normal twelve found in related species.
facts.quote: The describers established a single autapomorphy, unique trait: the possession of thirteen dorsal vertebrae instead of the normal twelve

facts.statement: The first four pairs of teeth in Barbosania are extremely long, forming a rosette adapted for catching slippery prey like fish or squids.
facts.quote: The first four tooth pairs are extremely long, forming a rosette to catch slippery prey like fish or squids

facts.statement: Barbosania was originally assigned to the superfamily Ornithocheiroidea and the family Ornithocheiridae.
facts.quote: Barbosania was assigned to the Ornithocheiroidea sensu Unwin and more precisely to the Ornithocheiridae

facts.statement: In 2019, Pêgas et al. reclassified Barbosania into the clade Targaryendraconia and the family Targaryendraconidae.
facts.quote: In 2019, Pêgas et al. assigned Barbosania to the clade Targaryendraconia, more specifically to the family Targaryendraconidae

facts.statement: Fossil evidence places Barbosania in existence between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (119.57 to 113.2 million years ago)
